That does not preclude advertisements containing offers to distribute general information on health-related matters, such as leaflets or information packs.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.13.1

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: No advertisement may encourage indiscriminate, unnecessary or excessive use of products or services covered by this section.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.14

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Advertisements should not falsely claim that a product is able to prevent or treat disease or a malformation; restore, correct or modify a physiological function; or modify a person’s appearance.* (This rule reflects a prohibited practice from Schedule 20 of the DMCCA. See note in Section 3 for more details).
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.15

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Unless authorised by the relevant product licence, the word "tonic" is not acceptable in advertisements that make health claims. Claims must not suggest that a product has tonic properties. That does not prevent the use of the word "tonic" in the description "Indian tonic water" or "quinine tonic water".
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.16

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Jingles may be used. Those that incorporate a medical or health claim must be substantiated.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.17

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Advertisements for smoking deterrents:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.18

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: must make clear that the indispensable factor in giving up smoking is willpower
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.18.1

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: must not claim that smoking is safer while the habit is being reduced. Harm reduction claims may be made, if authorised by the MHRA.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.18.2

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Medicines must have a licence from the MHRA, the VMD or under the auspices of the EMA before they are advertised. Advertisements for medicinal products must conform with the licence. Advertisements must not suggest that a product is "special" or "different" because it has been granted a licence from the MHRA. For the avoidance of doubt, by conforming with the product's indicated use, an advertisement would not breach rule 11.3.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.19

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Advertisements for medicinal products which include a product claim (including legible on-pack product claims within a pack shot) must include this information:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.20

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: the name of the product
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.20.1

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: the name of the active ingredient, if it contains only one
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.20.2

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: relevant wording such as "always read the label" or "always read the leaflet"
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.20.3

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: the indication (what the product is for). Advertisements for traditional herbal medicinal products and homeopathic medicinal products must include mandatory information, which can be found in the MHRA Blue Guide at: www.mhra.gov.uk . the indication (what the product is for). Advertisements for traditional herbal medicinal products and homeopathic medicinal products must include mandatory information, which can be found in the MHRA Blue Guide at: www.mhra.gov.uk .
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.20.4

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Advertisements for these are not acceptable:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.21

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: medicinal products or medical treatments available only on prescription
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.21.1

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Products for the treatment of alcohol or substance misuse or dependence. An exception is made for smoking deterrents (see rule 11.18).
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.21.2

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: No advertisement may suggest that a medicinal product is a foodstuff, cosmetic or other consumer product.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.22

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: No advertisement for a medicinal product may claim its effects are guaranteed. That does not prevent the offering of refunds, if the advertisement does not suggest that efficacy is guaranteed.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.23

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: No advertisement for a medicinal product or treatment may be directed at children. See also Section 5: Children and Section 32: Scheduling .
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.24

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Advertisements must not, without good reason, make the audience anxious that they are or might be suffering from disease or ill-health or might do so if they do not respond to the advertisement.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.25

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Advertisements must not falsely suggest that a product is necessary for the maintenance of physical or mental health or that health could be enhanced by taking the product or affected by not taking it.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.25.1

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Advertisements must not, in improper, alarming or misleading ways, use images of changes in the human body caused by disease, injury or a medicinal product.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.26

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: No advertisement for a medicinal product or treatment may include a recommendation by a person well-known in public life, sport, entertainment or similar or be presented by such a person. That includes persons corporate as well as singular and would prohibit, for example, recommendations by medical charities, patient groups and health or sport organisations.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.27

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: No advertisement for a medicinal product may refer in improper, alarming or misleading terms to claims of recovery.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.28

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Advertisements for medicinal products must not contain material that could, for example, by description or detailed representation of a case history, lead to a wrong self-diagnosis.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.29

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Although it may refer to the likely absence of a specific side effect, for example, "unlikely to cause drowsiness", no advertisement for a medicinal product may suggest that a product has no side effects.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.30

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: No advertisement for a medicinal product or treatment may suggest that the effects are better than, or equivalent to, those of another identifiable medicinal product or treatment.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.31

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: No advertisement for a medicinal product may suggest that the safety or efficacy of the product is due to it being "natural".
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.32

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Only homeopathic medicinal products that are registered in the UK may be advertised. Mandatory information for homeopathic advertisements can be found in the MHRA Blue Guide at: www.mhra.gov.uk .
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.33

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: A tension headache is a recognised medical condition; analgesics may be advertised for the relief of pain associated with that condition but no advertisement for a simple or compound analgesic may claim the direct relief of tension or refer to depression.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 11.34

metadata.section_title: 11 Medicines, medical devices, treatments and health

text: Radio Central Copy Clearance – Radio broadcasters must ensure advertisements subject to this Section are centrally cleared.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.1

text: If they are necessary for the assessment of claims, broadcasters must, before the advertisement is broadcast, obtain generally accepted scientific evidence and independent expert advice.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.2

text: Advertisements for services offering remote personalised advice on health matters related to weight control or slimming are acceptable only if all staff providing that advice are suitably qualified and subject to regulation by a statutory or recognised medical or health professional body and the advice given is in accordance with its relevant professional code of conduct (see rule 11.9). That does not prevent advertisements that offer general information on health matters related to slimming or weight control.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.3

text: Advertisements must not encourage indiscriminate or excessive use of a weight-control or slimming product or service.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.4

text: Advertisements for slimming or weight control products or services must not be addressed to people under 18, use creative treatments likely to be of particular appeal to them, or feature any person whose example people under 18 are likely to follow or who has a particular appeal to them. This rule does not apply to advertisements for calorie-reduced or energy-reduced foods and drinks, provided the product is not presented as part of a slimming regime and the advertisement does not use the theme of slimming or weight control.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.5

text: Broadcasters must obtain suitably qualified independent medical advice or other suitably qualified health specialist advice on the safety and efficacy of weight control and slimming products or services before broadcast. In particular, the advice must satisfy broadcasters that:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.6

text: the slimming product or service is likely to be effective and will not lead to harm
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.6.1

text: clinics and other establishments offering medically supervised treatments are run in accordance with the National Minimum Standards Regulations issued by the Department of Health or, if they operate abroad, broadly equivalent requirements.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.6.2

text: Promises or predictions of specific weight loss are not acceptable for any slimming product.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.7

text: Health claims in food product advertisements that refer to a rate or amount of weight loss are not permitted.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.8

text: Claims that refer to specific amounts of weight that have been lost by an individual must state the period over which that loss was achieved and should not be based on unrepresentative experiences of the slimming or weight-control product or service (see rule 12.8). The amount of weight lost and the period over which it was lost must be compatible with generally accepted good medical and dietary practice. For those who are normally overweight, a rate of weight loss greater than 2lbs (just under 1kg) a week is unlikely to be compatible with good medical and nutritional practice. For those who are obese, a rate of weight loss greater than 2lbs a week in the early stages of dieting could be compatible with good medical and nutritional practice.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.9

text: Low-calorie foods and drinks, if advertised as, or as part of, a slimming regime or if advertised using a slimming or weight-control theme, must make clear in the advertisement that the product merely helps weight loss as part of a calorie-controlled or energy-controlled diet.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.10

text: Except where stated in 12.11.1 and 12.11.2, advertisements for weight control or slimming products or services must not be targeted directly at individuals with a Body Mass Index of 30 or above (obesity) or use testimonials or case histories referring to subjects who were or seemed to be obese before using the advertised product.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.11

text: Advertisements for clinics or other establishments that offer treatment under suitably qualified medical supervision and advertisements for nonprescription medicines that are indicated for the treatment of obesity and that require the involvement of a pharmacist in the sale or supply of the medicine may nevertheless be targeted at those who are obese. Please see rule 11.9, "Services including Clinics, Establishments and the like Offering Advice on, or Treatment in, Medical, Personal or other Health Matters".
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.11.1

text: Lifestyle weight management programmes which meet the following standards may make responsible references to obesity in their advertisements. These programmes must: be shown to be effective at 12 months or beyond last at least three months be multi-component; addressing dietary intake, physical activity levels and behaviour change be developed by a multi-disciplinary team; including input from a registered dietitian, registered practitioner psychologist and a qualified physical activity instructor, and be provided by staff who are trained to deliver the programme in question. Advertisers should have regard to the guidance on ‘Managing overweight and obesity in adults – lifestyle weight management services’ published by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE). Lifestyle weight management programmes which meet the following standards may make responsible references to obesity in their advertisements. These programmes must: last at least three months be multi-component; addressing dietary intake, physical activity levels and behaviour change be developed by a multi-disciplinary team; including input from a registered dietitian, registered practitioner psychologist and a qualified physical activity instructor, and be provided by staff who are trained to deliver the programme in question.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.11.2

text: Advertisements for weight-control or slimming products must not suggest or imply that to be underweight is acceptable or desirable. If they are used, testimonials or case histories must not refer to subjects who are or seem to be underweight. Underweight, for the purpose of this rule, means a Body Mass Index below 20.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.12

text: Advertisements for specially formulated products intended for use in energy-restricted diets that, when used as instructed by the manufacturer, replace the whole of the total daily diet or one or more meals of the daily diet must comply with the Foods Intended for Use in Energy Restricted Diets For Weight Reduction Regulations 1997 (as amended), specifically:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.13

text: advertisements for such foods may not be offered under any name except "total diet replacement for weight control" or "meal replacement for weight control"
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.13.1

text: advertisements for such foods may not refer to the rate or amount of weight loss that could result from use of the product.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.13.2

text: For the purposes of this rule, very low-calorie diets (VLCDs) are those with a daily intake of less than 800 kilo-calories. They must comply with the provisions of the Food Safety Act 1990 and relevant regulations made under it, including those on advertising. These conditions apply to advertisements for such products:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.14

text: the advertisement must include a clear injunction to consult your doctor before embarking on the diet
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.14.1

text: the diet must be positioned as a short-term measure only
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.14.2

text: testimonials or specific case histories must not be used
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.14.3

text: independent medical advice must be sought on whether the proposed advertisement accords with the guidance on "Obesity: the prevention, identification, assessment and management of overweight and obesity in adults and children" (2006) published by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.14.4

text: Advertisements for establishments offering weight-control or slimming treatments are acceptable only if they make clear that dietary control is necessary to achieve weight loss. An exception is made for clinics and other establishments that provide immediate weight loss surgery under suitably qualified medical supervision and are run in accordance with rule 11.9. Those clinics and establishments must not refer to the amount of weight that can be lost.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 12.15

text: Radio Central Copy Clearance – Radio broadcasters must ensure advertisements subject to this Section are centrally cleared.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must avoid anything likely to condone or encourage poor nutritional habits or an unhealthy lifestyle, especially in children.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.2

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must not condone or encourage damaging oral healthcare practices, especially in children.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.2.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must not condone or encourage excessive consumption of any food.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.3

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Only nutrition claims listed in the applicable register are permitted in advertisements. Only health claims listed as authorised in the applicable register or claims that would have the same meaning for the audience may be used in advertisements.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.4

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Nutrition claims must comply with the criteria in the applicable register.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.4.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements that contain nutrition or health claims must be supported by documentary evidence to show they meet the conditions of use associated with the relevant claim, as specified in the applicable register. Advertisements must not give a misleading impression of the nutrition or health benefits of the product as a whole and factual nutrition statements should not imply a nutrition or health claim that cannot be supported. Claims must be presented clearly and without exaggeration
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.4.2

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: References to general benefits of a nutrient or food for overall good health or health-related well-being are acceptable only if accompanied by a specific authorised health claim
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.4.3

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Claims of a nutrition or health benefit that gives rise to doubt the safety or nutritional adequacy of another product are unacceptable.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.4.4

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Comparisons between foods must not discourage the selection of options such as fresh fruit and fresh vegetables, which generally accepted dietary opinion recommends should form a greater part of the average diet. Advertisements must not disparage good dietary practice. No advertisement should suggest that a balanced and varied diet cannot provide adequate nutrients in general
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.5

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Comparative nutrition claims must compare the difference in the claimed nutrient to a range of foods of the same category which do not have the composition that allows them to bear a nutrition claim
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.5.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: An advertisement may use one product as the sole reference for comparison only if that product is representative of the products in its category
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.5.2

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: The difference in the quantity of a nutrient or energy value must be stated in the advertisement and must relate to the same quantity of food.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.5.3

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: These are not acceptable in advertisements for products subject to this section:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.6

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Claims that state or imply health could be affected by not consuming a food
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.6.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Claims that state or imply a food prevents, treats or cures human disease. Reduction-of-disease-risk claims are acceptable if authorised by the applicable register
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.6.2

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Health claims that refer to the recommendation of an individual health professional. Health claims that refer to the recommendation of an association are acceptable only if that association is a health-related charity or a national representative body of medicine, nutrition or dietetics
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.6.3

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: References to changes in bodily functions that could give rise to or exploit fear in the audience
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.6.4

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Health claims that refer to a rate or amount of weight loss.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.6.5

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must not state or imply that a balanced and varied diet cannot provide appropriate quantities of nutrients in general. Individuals must not be encouraged to swap a healthy diet for supplementation.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.7

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Nutrition and health claims for food supplements must be permitted or authorised as provided for at rule 13.4 above. Advertisements that contain Nutrition or health claims must be supported by documentary evidence to show they meet the conditions of use associated with the relevant claim, as specified by the applicable register.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.7.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements for infant formula are prohibited.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.8

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must not confuse between infant formula and follow-on formula.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.8.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Television only – Promotional offers must be used with a due sense of responsibility. They may not be used in HFSS product advertisements targeted directly at pre-school or primary school children.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.9

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements featuring a promotional offer linked to a food product of interest to children must avoid creating a sense of urgency or encouraging the purchase of an excessive quantity for irresponsible consumption
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.9.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must not seem to encourage children to eat or drink a product only to take advantage of a promotional offer: the product should be offered on its merits, with the offer as an added incentive. Advertisements featuring a promotional offer should ensure a significant presence for the product
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.9.2

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements for collection-based promotions must not seem to urge children or their parents to buy excessive quantities of food. They must not directly encourage children only to collect promotional items, emphasise the number of items to be collected or create a sense of urgency. If a promotional offer can also be bought, that must be made clear. Closing dates for collection-based promotions must enable the whole set to be collected without having to buy excessive or irresponsible quantities of the product in a short time
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.9.3

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must not encourage children to eat more than they otherwise would. The notion of excessive or irresponsible consumption relates to the frequency of consumption as well as the amount consumed.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.9.4

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Television only – Licensed characters and celebrities popular with children must be used with a due sense of responsibility. They may not be used in HFSS product advertisements targeted directly at pre-school or primary school children. That prohibition does not apply to advertiser-created equity brand characters (puppets, persons or characters), which may be used by advertisers to sell the products they were designed to sell. Licensed characters and celebrities popular with children may present factual and relevant generic statements about nutrition, safety, education or similar. text: Television only – No nutrition or health claim may be used in HFSS product advertisements targeted directly at pre-school or primary school children. For the avoidance of doubt, claims referring to children's development or health are acceptable in non-HFSS product advertisements, if those claims are authorised on the applicable register.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.11

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Television only – Although children might be expected to exercise some preference over the food they eat or drink, advertisements must be prepared with a due sense of responsibility and must not directly advise or ask children to buy or to ask their parents or other adults to make enquiries or purchases for them. (Please see rule 5.9 in Section 5: Children )
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.12

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Nothing in an advertisement may seem to encourage children to pester or make a nuisance of themselves
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.12.1

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must not imply that children will be inferior to others, disloyal or will have let someone down, if they or their family do not buy, consume or use a product or service
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.12.2

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements must neither try to sell to children by appealing to emotions such as pity, fear, loyalty or self-confidence nor suggest that having the advertised product somehow confers superiority, for example, making a child more confident, clever, popular or successful
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.12.3

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Advertisements addressed to children must not urge children to buy or persuade others to buy and must avoid high-pressure or hard-sell techniques. Neither the words used nor the tone of the advertisement should suggest that young viewers could be bullied, cajoled or otherwise put under pressure to acquire the advertised item
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.12.4

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: If an advertisement for a children's product contains a price, the price must not be minimised by the use of words such as "only" or "just".
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.12.5

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

text: Radio only – Promotional offers to children must be used with a due sense of responsibility. They may not be used in food or soft drink product advertisements targeted directly at pre-school or primary school children; that prohibition does not apply to advertisements for fresh fruit or fresh vegetables. Advertisements that contain a promotional offer linked to a food or drink product of interest to children must neither seem to encourage children to eat or drink a product only to take advantage of a promotional offer nor create a sense of urgency. If a promotional item can also be bought, that must be made clear. Closing dates for collection-based promotions must enable the whole set to be collected without having to buy excessive or irresponsible quantities of the product in a short time.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.13

metadata.section_title: 13 Food, food supplements and associated health or nutrition claims

Licensed characters, equity brand characters or celebrities well-known to children may present factual and relevant generic statements about nutrition, safety, education and the like. citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 13.15

text: Radio Central Copy Clearance – Radio broadcasters must ensure advertisements for consumer credit, investment and complex financial products and services are centrally cleared.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.1

text: Broadcasters are responsible for ensuring that advertisements carried by them comply with all the relevant legal and regulatory requirements. Broadcasters might need to seek legal advice if an advertiser claims an advertisement should be considered:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.2

text: not to be a financial promotion or
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.2.1

text: to be a financial promotion that is not required to be communicated or approved by an authorised person (because it is subject to an exemption under the FPO). Advice, or general advice from the FCA, might be required on compliance with the FCA Handbook. The FCA does not pre-vet or advise on the compliance of proposed financial promotions with FSMA. For more information, visit the financial promotions pages of the FCA website ( www.fca.gov.uk ) and see the FCA Handbook, especially: the Consumer Credit sourcebook (CONC) Chapter 3; the Conduct of Business sourcebook (COBS) Chapter 4; the Mortgages and Home Finance: Conduct of Business sourcebook (MCOB) Chapter 3; the Insurance: Conduct of Business sourcebook (ICOBS) Chapter 2.2; and the Perimeter Guidance Manual (PERG) Chapter 8.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.2.2

text: Advertisements for financial services that are broadcast exclusively to audiences in EU Member States other than the UK or are not subject to the FCA's financial promotion rules need not comply with this section. Instead, they must comply with the laws and regulations of the relevant Member States.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.3

text: Financial promotions or other advertisements for regulated activities may be broadcast if:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.4

text: communicated by an authorised person
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.4.1

text: approved or issued by an authorised person or an appointed representative of an authorised person who, to the broadcaster's satisfaction, has confirmed that the final recorded version of the advertisement complies with the FCA's financial promotion rules or
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.4.2

text: exempt under the FPO. An advertisement by a general insurance intermediary need not be approved by an authorised person if it is a generic promotion and exempted by the FPO. (That is usually if the advertisement does not identify an insurer, insurance intermediary or product; so it will usually apply if the financial promotion refers generally to product types.)
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.4.3

text: These categories of advertisement may be broadcast on specialised financial channels, stations or programming only:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.5

text: advertisements for the acquisition or disposal of derivatives, warrants or other transferable securities (such as shares) that are not on the Official List of the FCA or admitted to trading on a Regulated Market in the UK or other EEA State (as defined by the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive)
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.5.1

text: advertisements for spread betting, as an investment only. Spread betting advertisements may be advertised on interactive or additional TV services (including text services). They must comply with the gambling rules (see Section 17: Gambling ). The advertised products or services should be available only to clients who have demonstrated through a pre-vetting procedure compliant with the FCA's appropriateness test that they have relevant financial trading experience
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.5.2

text: advertisements for contracts for differences (except spread betting), provided the products are available only to clients who have demonstrated through an appropriate pre-vetting procedure that they have relevant financial trading experience.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.5.3

text: advertisements for investment products not regulated or permitted under FSMA that are (or are presented as) conventional investments (in the sense that a consumer may invest money wit the expectation of a return). An advertisement that implies, for example, that a collectors' item or other unregulated product or service could have investment potential (in the colloquial sense) would normally be unacceptable.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.5.4

text: advertisements for cryptoassets that are transferable and fungible. See FCA guidance on qualifying cryptoassets for more information. The advertised products or services should be available only to clients who have demonstrated through a pre-vetting procedure compliant with the FCA's appropriateness test that they have relevant financial trading experience.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.5.5

text: Unless they are obviously addressed to a specialist audience and shown either on specialised financial channels or stations or in breaks in relevant financial programmes, advertisements subject to this section must be considered to be addressed to non-specialist audiences. No specialist knowledge should normally be required for a clear understanding of claims or references. For example, exceptions, conditions or expressions that would be understood by finance specialists must be avoided or explained if they would be unfamiliar to the audience.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.6

text: References to interest payable on savings are acceptable, subject to these conditions:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.7

text: they must be factually accurate at the time of broadcast and the advertisement must be modified immediately if the rate changes
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.7.1

text: advertisements quoting a rate must use the Annual Equivalent Rate (AER) and the contractual rate as set out in the British Bankers' Association and Building Societies Association Code of Conduct for the Advertising of Interest Bearing Accounts and advertisements should comply with all the provisions of that code
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.7.2

text: if conditions apply to calculations of interest and might affect the sum received, the advertisement must refer to the conditions and how they can be accessed
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.7.3

text: advertisements quoting a rate must make clear whether it is gross or net of tax, or tax-free, but do not need to explain those expressions
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.7.4

text: where the interest rate is variable, this must be stated
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.7.5

text: if the investment returns of different types of savings products are compared (for example, a unit trust and a bank deposit), significant differences between the products must be explained.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.7.6

text: Subject to legal requirements, reference to specific sums assured in life insurance advertisements must be accompanied by all relevant qualifying conditions; for example, age and gender of the assured at the outset of the policy, period of policy and amount and number of premiums payable.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.8

text: References to income tax and other tax benefits must be properly qualified, clarifying their meaning and making clear, if relevant, that the tax treatment depends on the individual circumstances of each person and could be subject to change in future.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.9

text: Advertisements for paper or electronic publications (for example, periodicals, books and text services) must not recommend a specific investment offer.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.10

text: The advertising of unsecured consumer credit or hire services by consumer credit businesses or consumer hire businesses and / or credit brokering  businesses or related credit services, such as debt counselling or debt adjusting is acceptable only if the advertiser complies with the financial promotions requirements imposed by FSMA and the FCA's rules set out in Chapter 3 of CONC..  The requirements for financial promotions set out in Chapter 3 of CONC do not apply: (a) where the credit is available only to a company or other body corporate (such as a limited liability partnership); (b) where a financial promotion is solely promoting credit agreements or consumer hire agreements or P2P lending agreements for the purposes of a customer's business; (c) to a financial promotion to the extent that it relates to qualifying credit or (d) it falls within the definition of an excluded communication as set out in the FCA's handbook. If the applicability or interpretation of these rules or provisions is in doubt, advertisers may contact the FCA. The FCA does not check financial promotions for compliance with the CONC rules before they are published. Such advertisements that involve distance marketing must also comply with the Financial Services (Distance Marketing) Regulations 2004 (as amended). Other distance-marketing financial advertisements are covered by the FCA Handbook.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.11

text: Advertisements for mortgages and re-mortgages are normally financial promotions under FSMA and must comply with the requirements imposed by FSMA and MCOB.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.12

text: Advertisements for most loans secured by a second charge are financial promotions, and special note should therefore be taken of the requirements of MCOB 3A.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.12.1

text: Advertisements for some mortgages might also have to comply with the provisions of COBS (for example if an investment product is being sold alongside a mortgage).
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.12.2

text: Advertisements on television or radio are unacceptable if they directly or indirectly invite the remittance of money direct to the advertiser or any other person without offering an opportunity to receive more information; an intermediate stage at which more information is supplied is mandatory.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.14

text: Advertisements on Ofcom-regulated text services that invite the direct remittance of money are acceptable for the categories listed in rule 14.4, but not those in rule 14.5.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 14.15

text: Radio Central Copy Clearance – Radio advertisements subject to this section must be centrally cleared.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.1

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Broadcasters must not accept advertisements from or on behalf of bodies:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.2

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: that practise or advocate illegal behaviour or
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.2.1

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: whose rites or other forms of collective observance are not normally directly accessible to the general public or
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.2.2

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: that apply unreasonable pressure on people to join or participate or not to opt out.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.2.3

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Broadcasters must be satisfied that no representatives will contact respondents without their consent.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.3

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Television advertisements must not promote psychic practices or practices related to the occult, except those permitted by rule 15.5. Radio advertisements may promote psychic and occult practices but must not make efficacy claims. Psychic and occult-related practices include ouija, satanism, casting of spells, palmistry, attempts to contact the dead, divination, clairvoyance, clairaudience, the invocation of spirits or demons and exorcism.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.4

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Television only – Subject to rules 15.5.1 and 15.5.2, television advertisements may promote services that the audience is likely to regard merely as entertainment and that offer generalised advice that would obviously be applicable to a large section of the population, for example, typical newspaper horoscopes.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.5

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements may promote a pre-recorded tarot-based prediction service if:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.5.1

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: the service includes no content that respondents might feel to be threatening and
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.5.1.a

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: both the advertisement and the service state clearly that the service is pre-recorded and qualify references to "tarot" to make clear that the predictions are not based on live readings.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.5.1.b

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements for personalised and live services that rely on belief in astrology, horoscopes, tarot and derivative practices are acceptable only on channels that are licensed for the purpose of the promotion of such services and are appropriately labelled: both the advertisement and the product or service itself must state that the product or service is for entertainment purposes only.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.5.2

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertising permitted under rule 15.5 may not:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.5.3

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must identify the advertiser and its faith, if that is not obvious from the context.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.6

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Television and television text advertisements must not expound doctrines or beliefs, unless they are broadcast on channels whose editorial content is wholly or mainly concerned with matters of religion, faith or equivalent systems of belief ("specialist broadcasters"). Advertisements carried by specialist broadcasters may express the advertiser's opinion on matters of doctrine or belief but must not present it as unqualified fact and must make clear to the audience that it is the advertiser's opinion. Radio advertisements may expound doctrines or beliefs if they are presented as the advertiser's opinion.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.7

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must not exhort audience members to change their beliefs or behaviour.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.8

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must not refer to the alleged consequences of faith or lack of faith. They must not present the advertiser's beliefs as the "one" or "true" faith.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.9

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must not denigrate the beliefs of others.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.10

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must not appeal for funds, except for charitable purposes. If the charitable purpose includes or will be accompanied by recruitment or evangelism, the advertisement must make that clear. Before broadcasting an advertisement that includes a charitable appeal, broadcasters must seek to be satisfied that the funds raised will be used solely for the benefit of specified groups. Advertisements must not imply that respondents will receive spiritual benefits in return for a donation to the advertised cause.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.11

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must not exploit the hopes or fears of the vulnerable. The elderly, the sick and the bereaved should be regarded as especially vulnerable.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.12

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must not claim that faith healing, miracle working or faith-based counselling can treat, cure or alleviate physical or mental health problems; they may, however, make restrained and proportionate claims that such services can benefit emotional or spiritual well-being.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.13

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must not appeal particularly to people under 18 and must not be broadcast during or adjacent to programmes that appeal or are likely to appeal particularly to those under 18. This rule does not apply to advertisements for public events, including services and festivals, that children are likely to participate in or to advertisements for publications or similar merchandise that are designed for children, provided that neither the advertisement nor the advertised product or service is linked to recruitment or fundraising. It does not apply to advertisements on channels or stations whose editorial content is dedicated to matters of religion, faith or equivalent systems of belief.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.14

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Advertisements must not feature children as presenters, unless the advertisement is for an event, such as Christmas carol services or Diwali celebrations, that children are especially likely to take part in.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 15.15

metadata.section_title: 15 Faith, religion and equivalent systems of belief

text: Radio Central Copy Clearance – Radio broadcasters must ensure advertisements subject to this section are centrally cleared.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.1

text: Advertising is acceptable only from:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.2

text: bodies registered with the relevant UK authorities as having charitable status or bodies that have had their charitable status otherwise officially recognised, for example by HM Revenue & Customs: index.htm .
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.2.1

text: bodies based outside the UK that supply to broadcasters confirmation that they comply with all relevant legislation in their home countries and evidence of their good faith, which might include audited accounts and a list of members of their governing body.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.2.2

text: Advertisements seeking donations for, or promoting the needs or objectives of a charitable body must not:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.3

text: misrepresent the body, its activities or the benefits of donated funds or exaggerate the scale or nature of the cause it claims to support
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.3.1

text: suggest that anyone will lack proper feeling or fail in a responsibility by not supporting a charity
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.3.2

text: disrespect the dignity of those on whose behalf an appeal is being made
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.3.3

text: address fund-raising messages to children or likely to be of particular interest to them.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.3.4

text: If the advertisement states that payment may be made by credit or debit card, the donor's right to have any payment of £100 or more refunded must be stated.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.4

text: Advertisements by non-charity advertisers which promote the needs or objects of charitable bodies, or offer to assist them, are only acceptable if the bodies would be acceptable advertisers in their own right under rule 16.2.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.5

text: Advertisements that include an offer to donate money to charity must:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.6

text: not depend on sales reaching a given level or be subject to a similar condition. If a target total or an amount for each purchase is stated, any extra money given to the charity must be donated on the same basis as contributions below that level
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.6.1

text: identify the charity that will benefit and state the basis on which the contribution will be calculated (in accordance with rule 16.9) and, where more than one charity is involved, the advertisement may give a generic identification but should be accompanied by a statement listing the charities and the proportions in which they will benefit.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.6.2

text: Broadcasters must hold evidence that each charity has agreed to the proposed advertisement
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.7

text: Advertisements for medicinal products may offer to donate money to charity but must not be likely to encourage indiscriminate, unnecessary or excessive purchases of medicinal products. Advertisements must state the basis on which the contribution will be calculated. See also Section 11: Medicines, Medical Devices, Treatments and Health
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.8

text: Where a promotion states or implies that part of the price paid for goods or services will be given to a charity or cause, the advertisement must state the actual amount or percentage of the price that will be paid to the charity or cause, for example, "£1 per sale" or "10% of the purchase price".
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.9

text: For any other promotion linked to a charity or where a third party states or implies that donations will be given to a charity or cause, the advertisement must state the total (or a reasonable estimate) of the amount the charity or cause will receive.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 16.9.1

text: Radio Central Copy Clearance – Radio broadcasters must ensure that advertisements for gambling are centrally cleared.

text: Advertisements for events or facilities that can be accessed only by entering gambling premises must make that condition clear.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.2

text: Advertisements must not:

text: portray, condone or encourage gambling behaviour that is socially irresponsible or could lead to financial, social or emotional harm
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.3.1

text: suggest that gambling can provide an escape from personal, professional or educational problems such as loneliness or depression
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.3.2

text: suggest that gambling can be a solution to financial concerns, an alternative to employment or a way to achieve financial security
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.3.3

text: portray gambling as indispensable or as taking priority in life; for example, over family, friends or professional or educational commitments

text: suggest peer pressure to gamble or disparage abstention
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.3.5

text: link gambling to seduction, sexual success or enhanced attractiveness
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.3.7

text: portray gambling in a context of toughness or link it to resilience or recklessness
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.3.8

text: suggest gambling is a rite of passage
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.3.9

text: suggest that solitary gambling is preferable to social gambling.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.3.10

text: exploit cultural beliefs or traditions about gambling or luck
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.4.1

text: condone or encourage criminal or anti-social behaviour
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.4.2

text: condone or feature gambling in a working environment (an exception exists for licensed gambling premises)
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.4.3

text: exploit the susceptibilities, aspirations, credulity, inexperience or lack of knowledge of under-18s or other vulnerable persons
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 17.4.4

text: be likely to be of strong appeal to children or young persons, especially by reflecting or being associated with youth culture. Where appropriate steps have been taken to limit the potential for an advertisement to appeal strongly to under-18s, this rule does not prevent the advertising of gambling products associated with activities that are themselves of strong appeal to under-18s (for instance, certain sports or playing video games). text: feature anyone who is, or seems to be, under 25 years old gambling or playing a significant role. No-one may behave in an adolescent, juvenile or loutish way.

text: Advertisements for family entertainment centres, travelling fairs, horse racecourses and dog racetracks, and for non-gambling leisure facilities that incidentally refer to separate gambling facilities as part of a list of facilities on, for example, a cruise ship, may include under-18s provided they are accompanied by an adult and are socialising responsibly in areas that the Gambling Act 2005 (as amended) does not restrict by age.

text: Advertisements for lotteries that can be participated in only by entering gambling premises must make that condition clear.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 18.3

text: Advertisements for lotteries must not exploit the susceptibilities, aspirations, credulity, inexperience or lack of knowledge of under-18s or other vulnerable persons.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 18.4

text: Advertisements for lotteries must not be likely to be of strong appeal to children or young persons, especially by reflecting or being associated with youth culture. They must not include a person or character whose example is likely to be followed by those aged under 18 years or who has a strong appeal to those aged under 18. Where the subject of a lotteries product (for example, good causes benefitting from lottery funds) or features of the product itself (for example, the creative content, gameplay or a prize involved) are of strong appeal to under-18s, an advertisement for that lottery may depict the subject and/or product, but it must not feature a person or character whose example is likely to be followed by those aged under 18 years or who has a strong appeal to those aged under 18. Lotteries advertisements that solely depict the good causes supported by the lottery may include persons or characters whose example is likely to be followed by those aged under 18 years or who has a strong appeal to those aged under 18 provided that: a)they are directly associated with the lottery good cause (for example, an athlete who has received lottery funding directly); b)there is no explicit encouragement to purchase a lottery product; and c)there is no reference to scratchcards or online instant-win lottery products. Lotteries advertisements including product references that comply with rule 18.7.2 are also acceptable. Please refer to Section 32 for scheduling restrictions. text: Radio Central Copy Clearance – Radio broadcasters must ensure advertisements for alcoholic drinks are centrally cleared.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.1

text: Advertisements must not feature, imply, condone or encourage irresponsible or immoderate drinking. That applies to both the amount of drink and the way drinking is portrayed. References to, or suggestions of, buying repeat rounds of alcoholic drinks are not acceptable. That does not prevent, for example, someone buying a drink for each member of a group. It does, however, prevent any suggestion that other members of the group will buy a round.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.2

text: Advertisements must neither imply that alcohol can contribute to an individual's popularity or confidence nor imply that alcohol can enhance personal qualities
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.3

text: Advertisements must not imply that drinking alcohol is a key component of social success or acceptance or that refusal is a sign of weakness. Advertisements must not imply that the success of a social occasion depends on the presence or consumption of alcohol.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.4

text: Advertisements must not link alcohol with daring, toughness, aggression or unruly, irresponsible or antisocial behaviour.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.5

text: Advertisements must not link alcohol with sexual activity, sexual success or seduction or imply that alcohol can enhance attractiveness. That does not preclude linking alcohol with romance or flirtation.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.6

text: Advertisements must not portray alcohol as indispensable or as taking priority in life. Advertisements must not imply that drinking can overcome problems or that regular solitary drinking is acceptable
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.7

text: Advertisements must not imply that alcohol has therapeutic qualities. Alcohol must not be portrayed as capable of changing mood, physical condition or behaviour or as a source of nourishment. Although they may refer to refreshment, advertisements must not imply that alcohol can improve any type of performance.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.8

text: Advertisements must not link alcohol to illicit drugs.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.9

text: Advertisements may give factual information about the alcoholic strength of a drink. They may also make a factual alcohol strength comparison with another product, but only when the comparison is with a higher-strength product of a similar beverage. Advertisements must not imply that a drink may be preferred because of its alcohol content or intoxicating effect. However, low-alcohol drinks may be presented as preferable because of their low alcoholic strength, provided that the alcohol content of the drink is stated clearly in the advertisement. In the case of a drink with relatively high alcoholic strength in relation to its category, the factual information should not be given undue emphasis. Advertisements may give factual information about the alcoholic strength of a drink. They may also make a factual alcohol strength comparison with another product, but only when the comparison is with a higher-strength product of a similar beverage. Advertisements must not imply that a drink may be preferred because of its alcohol content or intoxicating effect. However, low-alcohol drinks may be presented as preferable because of their low alcoholic strength, provided that the alcohol content of the drink is stated clearly in the advertisement. In the case of a drink with relatively high alcoholic strength in relation to its category, the factual information should not be given undue emphasis.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.10

text: Advertisements may include alcohol promotions but must not imply, condone or encourage immoderate drinking.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.11

text: Advertisements must not feature alcohol being handled or served irresponsibly.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.12

text: Advertisements must not link alcohol with the use of potentially dangerous machinery or driving. Advertisements may feature sporting and other physical activities (subject to other rules in this section) but must not imply that those activities have been undertaken after the consumption of alcohol.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.13

text: Advertisements must not normally show alcohol being drunk by anyone in their working environment.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.14

text: Television only – Alcohol advertisements must not:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.15

text: be likely to appeal strongly to people under 18, especially by reflecting or being associated with youth culture or showing adolescent or juvenile behaviour
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.15.1

text: include a person or character whose example is likely to be followed by those aged under 18 years or who has a strong appeal to those aged under 18.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.15.2

text: Radio only – Alcohol advertisements must not:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.16

text: be targeted at those under 18 years or use a treatment likely to be of particular appeal to them.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.16.1

text: include a person or character whose example is likely to be followed by those aged under 18 years or who has a particular appeal to those aged under 18.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.16.2

text: Alcohol advertisements must not feature in a significant role anyone who is, or seems to be, under 25 and must not feature children. An exception is made for advertisements that feature families socialising responsibly. Here, children may be included but they should have an incidental role only and anyone who seems to be under the age of 25 must be obviously not drinking alcohol.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.17

text: Advertisements for alcoholic drinks may give factual statements about product contents, including comparisons, but must not make any health claims, which include fitness or weight-control claims. The only permitted nutrition claims are "low alcohol", "reduced alcohol" and "reduced energy" and any claim likely to have the same meaning for the audience.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.18

text: If an advertisement for an alcohol alternative refers to or depicts alcohol, those references or depictions must comply with the rules relating to responsible portrayal of alcohol consumption, which are 19.2-19.9 and 19.11-19.14. Where an advertisement is for an alcohol alternative that shares the same brand as an alcoholic drink then this rule will not apply to references to or depictions of the brand name, provided that the primary effect of the advertisement is to promote the alcohol alternative. References to the shared brand name, in any part of the advertisement, without a reference to the alcohol alternative, are likely to be understood as references to alcohol.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.19

text: Advertisements for alcohol alternatives must include a prominent statement of their ABV. Advertisements for alcohol alternatives are not prohibited from making a feature of their ABV or from making preference claims on this basis.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.20

text: Advertisements for alcohol alternatives may depict the product in circumstances where consumption of alcoholic drinks would be inappropriate or unsafe – such as prior to driving or daring physical activities – if it is clear the product is an alcohol alternative. Advertisements must not encourage or condone consumption of alcohol in the same circumstances or imply the product is alcoholic. Resemblance to an alcoholic drink (as in rule 19.19) is acceptable as long as the ad makes explicitly clear the product featured is an alcohol alternative.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.21

text: Advertisements for alcohol alternatives must not contain content likely to disparage sobriety, or condone or encourage heavy, problematic, or otherwise higher-risk alcohol consumption as desirable. They must not present alcohol alternatives as a way to increase alcohol consumption beyond responsible levels.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.22

text: Television only – Alcohol alternatives advertisements must not:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.23

text: be likely to appeal strongly to people under 18, especially by reflecting or being associated with youth culture or showing adolescent or juvenile behaviour.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.23.1

text: include a person or character whose example is likely to be followed by those aged under 18 years or who has a strong appeal to those aged under 18.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.23.2

text: Radio only – Alcohol alternatives advertisements must not:
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.24

text: be targeted at those under 18 years or use a treatment likely to be of particular appeal to them.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.24.1

text: include a person or character whose example is likely to be followed by those aged under 18 years or who has a particular appeal to those aged under 18.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.24.2

text: Alcohol alternatives advertisements must not feature in a significant role anyone who is, or seems to be, under 25 and must not feature children. An exception is made for advertisements that feature families socialising responsibly. Here, children may be included but they should have an incidental role only and anyone who seems to be under the age of 25 must be obviously not drinking alcohol or alcohol alternatives.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 19.25

text: Advertisements must not condone or encourage dangerous, competitive, inconsiderate or irresponsible driving or motorcycling. Advertisements must not suggest that driving or motorcycling safely is staid or boring.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 20.1

text: Advertisements must not condone or encourage a breach of the legal requirements of the Highway Code.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 20.2

text: Motoring advertisements must not demonstrate power, acceleration or handling characteristics except in a clear context of safety. Reference to those characteristics must not suggest excitement, aggression or competitiveness.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 20.3

text: Motoring advertisements must not refer to speed in a way that might condone or encourage dangerous, competitive, inconsiderate or irresponsible driving or motorcycling. Factual statements about a vehicle's speed or acceleration are permissible but must not be presented as a reason for preferring the advertised vehicle. Speed or acceleration claims must not be the main selling message of an advertisement.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 20.4

text: Motoring advertisements must not exaggerate the benefit of safety features to consumers or suggest that a vehicle's features enable it to be driven or ridden faster or in complete safety.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 20.5

text: Radio Central Copy Clearance – Radio advertisements for betting tipsters must be centrally cleared.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.1

text: Advertisements for betting tipsters must not be likely to be of particular appeal to under-18s.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.2

text: Advertisements for betting tipster services must not make money-back guarantees.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.3

text: Advertisements for betting tipster update-line services are acceptable only if the broadcaster is satisfied that the recorded messages are brief and the lines are a valid and necessary complement to the main-line service.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.4

text: Before broadcasting an advertisement for a betting tipster service, a broadcaster must hold the tipster's name (not merely his or her business name) and his or her full, permanent business address.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.5

text: Advertisements for a betting tipster service operating on a premium-rate phone line must include the service provider or information provider's usual trading name and contact details (see Section 22: Premium-rate Telephone Services ).
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.6

text: Advertisements for betting tipsters who run, or are associated with, another betting tipster service must make that link clear.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.7

text: Advertisements may include claims about a betting tipster's previous successful tips only if those claims are supported, before the relevant race, by proofing of all tips offered on his or her service on the day or during the period in question.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.8

text: Advertisements for betting tipsters must not include claims about notional profits. Claims about previous profits must be proportionate and representative.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.9

text: Advertisements for betting tipsters must not state or imply that success is guaranteed or that players could forge a long-term income by following the advertiser's tips.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.10

text: Advertisements for betting tipsters may include claims about previous successful double, treble or other combination bets only if those claims are supported by proofing that the winners were clearly and specially tipped as a combination.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.11

text: Profit, success or individual-win claims must not refer to odds.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.12

text: If a change in circumstance would render it misleading, for example, if a race meeting were cancelled, an advertisement for a betting tipster must be not be repeated in its original form.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.13

text: Advertisements for betting tipsters must not refer to a tip as a maximum bet or similar unless it is the only tip offered for that race. Claims about the success of a maximum tip are acceptable only if they are supported by advance proofing.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 21.14

text: Advertisements that include a premium-rate telephone number must comply with the Phone-paid Services Authority Code of Practice.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 22.1

text: Advertisements for premium-rate telephone services must include clear pricing information if the service generally costs 50 pence per call or more.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 22.2

text: Advertisements for premium-rate children's services, services accessed by automated equipment or subscription services must always include clear pricing information.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 22.3

text: Advertisements for premium-rate services must state the identity of the service provider or the information provider.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 22.4

text: Radio only – If it is not included in the advertisement, radio broadcasters must retain and, on request, make available a non-premium-rate telephone number for the premium-rate service for customer care purposes. This rule does not apply if the Phone-paid Services Authority has expressly exempted a specific service or a number range from the need to provide a non-premium-rate telephone number for the premium-rate service.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 22.5

text: Television only – Television advertisements for premium-rate services must include a non-premium-rate telephone number for customer care purposes. This rule does not apply if the Phone-paid Services Authority has expressly exempted a specific service or a number range from the need to provide a non-premium-rate telephone number for the premium-rate service.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 22.6

text: Advertisements for services, excluding live or virtual-chat services, that normally involve a telephone call of at least five minutes must alert the audience that use of the service might involve a long call.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 22.7

text: Advertisements for live premium-rate services must not appeal particularly to people under 18, unless those services have received prior permission from the Phone-paid Services Authority to target people under 18.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 22.8

text: To maintain a distinction between programmes and advertisements that is clear to a child audience, and to minimise any risk of confusion between the two, advertisements featuring a well-known personality or performer, or a person who takes a leading role in or whose appearance is central to a children's programme, must not be scheduled in breaks in or adjacent to that programme. For the purposes of this rule, cartoon and puppet characters are classed as "persons". For appearances by persons in chart programmes or programmes such as pop concerts, the restriction applies only to the breaks adjacent to the programme segment in which they appear. text: Advertisements for e-cigarettes must be socially responsible.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 33.1

text: Advertisements must contain nothing which promotes any design, imagery or logo style that might reasonably be associated in the audience's mind with a tobacco brand.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 33.2

text: Advertisements must contain nothing which promotes the use of a tobacco product or shows the use of a tobacco product in a positive light. This rule is not intended to prevent cigarette-like products being shown.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 33.3

text: Advertisements must make clear that the product is an e-cigarette and not a tobacco product.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 33.4

text: Advertisements must not contain medicinal claims unless the product is authorised for those purposes by the MHRA. E-cigarettes may be presented as an alternative to tobacco but marketers must do nothing to undermine the message that quitting tobacco use is the best option for health.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 33.5

text: Advertisements must not use health professionals to endorse electronic cigarettes. For the avoidance of doubt, this does not apply to public health campaigns (see rule 10.1.11).
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 33.6

text: This rule was deleted on 8 November 2018, following public consultation.

text: Advertisements must not encourage non-smokers or non-nicotine-users to use e-cigarettes.
citation: BCAP Code (Edition 12) rule 33.8

text: Advertisements must not be likely to appeal particularly to people under 18, especially by reflecting or being associated with youth culture. They should not feature or portray real or fictitious characters who are likely to appeal particularly to people under 18. People shown using e-cigarettes or playing a significant role should not be shown behaving in an adolescent or juvenile manner.

text: People shown using e-cigarettes or playing a significant role must neither be, nor seem to be, under 25. People under 25 may be shown in an incidental role but must be obviously not using e-cigarettes.
