commentary: S. 249 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: A person does not commit an offence under section 33 or 243(1) by reason only of the fact that he supplies, repairs, installs or maintains a gaming machine or part of a gaming machine in accordance with a permit under this section. A person may apply to the Commission for a permit authorising him to supply, repair, install or maintain a gaming machine or part of a gaming machine. An application under this section must— be made in writing, specify the gaming machine or part in relation to which the permit is sought, give such details of the activity in relation to which the permit is sought as the Commission may direct, be in such form, and contain such other information, as the Commission may direct, and be accompanied by the prescribed fee. On consideration of an application under this section the Commission may— grant the application and issue a permit to the applicant, or refuse the application. The Commission may grant an application under this section only if satisfied that the licensing objectives are irrelevant to the activity for which the permit is sought. A permit under this section must specify— a period, not exceeding one year, during which it has effect, the machine or part to which it relates, and the activities which it authorises. A permit under this section may be subject to a condition attached by the Commission. In subsection (3)(e) “prescribed” means prescribed by regulations made by the Secretary of State.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.250

commentary: S. 250 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: This Part applies— to anything done in relation to a gaming machine which (or any part of which) is situated in Great Britain, and to anything done in Great Britain in relation to a gaming machine (irrespective of where it is situated).
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.251

text: For the purposes of this Act a person promotes a lottery if he makes or participates in making the arrangements for a lottery. In particular, a person promotes a lottery if he— makes arrangements for the printing of lottery tickets, makes arrangements for the printing of promotional material, arranges for the distribution or publication of promotional material, possesses promotional material with a view to its distribution or publication, makes other arrangements to advertise a lottery, invites a person to participate in a lottery, sells or supplies a lottery ticket, offers to sell or supply a lottery ticket, possesses a lottery ticket with a view to its sale or supply, does or offers to do anything by virtue of which a person becomes a member of a class among whom prizes in a lottery are to be allocated, or uses premises for the purpose of allocating prizes or for any other purpose connected with the administration of a lottery. In subsection (2) “promotional material” means a document which— advertises a specified lottery, invites participation in a specified lottery, contains information about how to participate in a specified lottery, or lists winners in a specified lottery. Where arrangements for a lottery are made by an external lottery manager on behalf of a society or authority, for the purposes of this Act both the external lottery manager and the society or authority promote the lottery.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.252

text: For the purposes of this Act a document or article is a lottery ticket if it confers, or can be used to prove, membership of a class for the purpose of the allocation of prizes in a lottery. A reference in this Act to the sale or supply of a lottery ticket by a person includes a reference to a person doing anything as a result of which another person becomes a member of the class among whom prizes in a lottery are to be allocated. A reference in this Act to purchase of a lottery ticket includes a reference to any action by a person as a result of which he becomes a member of the class among whom prizes in a lottery are to be allocated.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.253

text: In this Act a reference to the proceeds of a lottery is a reference to the aggregate of amounts paid in respect of the purchase of lottery tickets. In this Act a reference to the profits of a lottery is a reference to— the proceeds of the lottery, minus amounts deducted by the promoters of the lottery in respect of— the provision of prizes, sums to be made available for allocation in another lottery in accordance with a rollover, or other costs reasonably incurred in organising the lottery.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.254

text: In this Act “draw”, in relation to a lottery, includes any process by which a prize in the lottery is allocated.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.255

text: In this Act “rollover” in relation to a lottery means an arrangement whereby the fact that a prize is not allocated or claimed in one lottery increases the value of the prizes available for allocation in another lottery. For the purposes of this Act where prizes are allocated by means of more than one draw— the draws together constitute a single lottery if the class of persons among whom prizes are allocated is (and, by virtue of arrangements for the sale or supply of tickets, must be) the same in the case of each draw, and otherwise, the arrangements for each draw constitute a separate lottery.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.256

text: A person acts as an external lottery manager for the purposes of this Act if he makes arrangements for a lottery on behalf of a society or authority of which he is not— a member, an officer, or an employee under a contract of employment.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.257

text: A person commits an offence if he promotes a lottery unless— the exception in subsection (2) or (3) applies, or the lottery is an exempt lottery. This section does not apply to activity by a person if— he holds an operating licence authorising the activity, and he acts in accordance with the terms and conditions of the licence. This section does not apply to activity by a person if— he acts, otherwise than as an external lottery manager, on behalf of a person who holds an operating licence authorising the activity, and the activity is carried on in accordance with the terms and conditions of the licence. It is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section to show that he reasonably believed that— he was not committing the offence by reason of subsection (1)(b), (2) or (3), that the arrangement to which the charge relates was not a lottery, or that the arrangement to which the charge relates was a lottery forming part of the National Lottery. In this Act “exempt lottery” means a lottery which is exempt by virtue of a provision of Schedule 11.

text: A person commits an offence if he facilitates a lottery unless— the exception in subsection (3) applies, or the lottery is an exempt lottery. For the purposes of this section a person facilitates a lottery if (and only if) he— prints lottery tickets for a specified lottery, prints promotional material for a specified lottery, or advertises a specified lottery. This section does not apply to activity by a person if he acts in accordance with the terms and conditions of an operating licence. It is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section to show that he reasonably believed— that he was not committing the offence by reason of subsection (1)(b) or (3), or that the arrangement to which the charge relates was not a lottery, or that the arrangement to which the charge relates was a lottery forming part of the National Lottery. In subsection (2)(b) “promotional material” means a document which— advertises a specified lottery, invites participation in a specified lottery, contains information about how to participate in a specified lottery, or lists winners in a specified lottery.

text: This section applies to a lottery in respect of which the promoter has stated (in whatever terms) a fund-raising purpose for the promotion of the lottery. The reference in subsection (2) to using profits includes a reference to permitting profits to be used. In subsection (1) the reference to a statement of a purpose for the promotion of a lottery is a reference to a statement appearing— on lottery tickets, or in an advertisement for the lottery. In subsection (4)(b) “advertisement” in relation to a lottery includes any written notice announcing that a lottery will take place or inviting people to participate in a lottery (in either case whether or not it also gives other information).

text: This section applies to the following kinds of lottery— an incidental ... lottery (within the meaning of Part 1 of Schedule 11), a private society lottery (within the meaning of Part 2 of that Schedule), ... a work lottery and a residents’ lottery (within the meaning of Part 2 of that Schedule) except where the lottery has been organised in such a way as to ensure that no profits are made, and a small society lottery (within the meaning of Part 4 of that Schedule). A person commits an offence if he uses any part of the profits of a lottery to which this section applies for a purpose other than one for which the lottery is permitted to be promoted in accordance with Schedule 11. text: In this Act members' club means a club— which is established and conducted wholly or mainly for purposes other than the provision of facilities for gaming (subject to subsection (2)), which is established and conducted for the benefit of its members (and which is not otherwise established or conducted as a commercial enterprise), which is not established with the purpose of functioning only for a limited period of time, and which has at least 25 individual members. A club is a members' club for the purposes of this Act despite subsection (1)(a) if— it is established or conducted wholly or mainly for the purpose of the provision of facilities for gaming of a prescribed kind, and facilities are not provided for any other kind of gaming in the course of the club's activities.

text: In this Act miners' welfare institute means an association— which is established and conducted for social and recreational purposes, and which satisfies subsection (2) or (4). An association satisfies this subsection if its affairs are managed by a group of individuals of whom at least two thirds are miners' representatives. In subsection (2) “miners' representative” means a person who— is nominated or appointed by a person who employs or has employed individuals in the course of a coal mining business, is nominated or appointed by the charitable trust known as the Coal Industry Social Welfare Organisation, is nominated or appointed by an organisation representing persons who are or were employed in connection with coal mining, or is or was employed in connection with coal mining; and the group mentioned in subsection (2) must contain both one or more persons of a kind specified in paragraph (a) or (b) and one or more persons of a kind specified in paragraph (c) or (d). An association satisfies this subsection if— it operates on premises the use of which is regulated in accordance with a charitable trust, and the trust has received money from— the Miners' Welfare Fund established by section 20 of the Mining Industry Act 1920 (c. 50), the former body corporate which was known as the Coal Industry Social Welfare Organisation and incorporated under the Companies Act 1948 (c. 38), or the charitable trust known as the Coal Industry Social Welfare Organisation.

text: Sections 33 and 37 shall not apply to the provision of facilities for equal chance gaming which satisfies the conditions of this section by— a members' club, a commercial club, a club that would be a members' club but for section 266(1)(a), a club that would be a commercial club but for section 267(1)(a), or a miners' welfare institute. The first condition of gaming for the purposes of subsection (1) is that the arrangements for the gaming satisfy the prescribed requirements (if any) in relation to— amounts that may be staked, or the amount or value of a prize. The second condition of gaming for the purposes of subsection (1) is that no amount is deducted or levied from sums staked or won. The third condition of gaming for the purposes of subsection (1) is that any participation fee does not exceed such maximum as may be prescribed. The fourth condition of gaming for the purposes of subsection (1) is that a game played on one set of premises is not linked with a game played on another set of premises. The fifth condition of gaming for the purposes of subsection (1), which does not apply to a club of a kind mentioned in subsection (1)(b) or (d), is that each person who participates— is a member of the club or institute who applied for membership, was nominated for membership or became a member, at least 48 hours before he participates, or is a guest of a member of the club or institute who would be entitled to participate by virtue of paragraph (a).

text: In section 269(1) a reference to the provision of facilities by a club or institute includes a reference to any provision of facilities made— on behalf of or by arrangement with the club or institute, and in the course of its activities. Regulations prescribing requirements in relation to stakes or prizes for the purposes of section 269(2) may, in particular— make different provision for different classes of club or institute; make different provision for different classes or descriptions of game. In section 269(3) the reference to a deduction or levy in respect of gaming provided by, on behalf of or by arrangement with a club or institute is to a deduction or levy made by or on behalf of— the club or institute, or a person providing facilities for gaming on behalf of, or by arrangement with, the club or institute. Regulations prescribing a maximum charge for the purposes of section 269(4) may, in particular— make different provision for different classes of club or institute; make provision depending on whether a club or institute holds a club gaming permit; make different provision for different classes or descriptions of game; make different provision for different classes or descriptions of fee. For the purposes of section 269(5) two games are linked if— the result of one game is or may be wholly or partly determined by reference to the result of the other game, or the amount of winnings available in one game is or may be wholly or partly determined by reference to the amount of participation in the other game; and if a single game is played partly on one set of premises and partly on another it shall be treated as two linked games. For the purposes of section 269(6) a person shall not be treated as the guest of a member if the member extends an invitation— having had no previous acquaintance with the person, and for the purpose only of enabling the person to take advantage of facilities for gaming provided by or for the club or institute.

text: Sections 33, 37 and 242 shall not apply to the provision of facilities for gaming in accordance with a club gaming permit. A club gaming permit is a permit issued by a licensing authority authorising the provision of facilities for gaming— on premises on which a members' club or a miners' welfare institute operates, and in the course of the activities of the club or institute. A club gaming permit shall, by virtue of this section, authorise— making up to three gaming machines available for use, each of which must be of Category B, C or D, the provision of facilities for gaming which satisfies the conditions in section 269 except for the first condition, and the provision of facilities for games of chance, of such class or description as may be prescribed, in accordance with the conditions specified in subsection (4). Those conditions are— that no participation fee is charged otherwise than in accordance with regulations (which may make provision about the circumstances in which a fee may be charged and about the amount of a fee), that no amount is deducted or levied from sums staked or won otherwise than in accordance with regulations (which may make provision about the circumstances in which an amount may be deducted or levied, about the amount of the deduction or levy and about the method by which the amount is determined), that the public is excluded from any area of the club's or institute's premises where gaming is taking place, and that children and young persons are excluded from any area of the club's or institute's premises where gaming is taking place. Regulations under subsection (4)(a) or (b) may— make different provision for different classes of club or institute; make different provision for different classes or descriptions of game; make different provision for different classes or descriptions of fee, deduction or levy. A club gaming permit shall, by virtue of this subsection, be subject to the condition that each person who participates in gaming in reliance on the permit— is a member of the club or institute who applied for membership, was nominated for membership or became a member, at least 48 hours before he participates, or is a guest of a member of the club or institute who would be entitled to participate by virtue of paragraph (a). A club gaming permit shall, by virtue of this subsection, be subject to the conditions— that no child or young person use a Category B or C gaming machine on the club's or institute's premises, and that the holder comply with any relevant provision of a code of practice under section 24 about the location and operation of a gaming machine.

text: For the purposes of section 271(4)(b) the reference to a deduction or levy in respect of gaming provided by, on behalf of or by arrangement with a club or institute is to a deduction or levy made by or on behalf of— the club or institute, or a person providing facilities for gaming on behalf of, or by arrangement with, the club or institute. In section 271(4)(c) “the public” means persons other than— members of the club or institute, guests of members of the club or institute, staff of the club or institute, and persons providing services to or for the club or institute. For the purposes of section 271(4)(c) and (d) a reference to an area where gaming is taking place is a reference to any place in which it is possible to participate in the gaming. text: Sections 37 and 242 shall not apply to making a gaming machine available for use in accordance with a club machine permit. A club machine permit is a permit issued by a licensing authority authorising up to three gaming machines, each of which must be of Category B, C or D, to be made available for use— on premises on which a members' club, a commercial club or a miners' welfare institute operates, and in the course of the activities of the club or institute. A club machine permit held by a members' club or a miners' welfare institute shall, by virtue of this subsection, be subject to the condition that each person to whom a machine is made available for use in reliance on the permit— is a member of the club or institute who applied for membership, was nominated for membership or became a member, at least 48 hours before he uses the machine, or is a guest of a member of the club or institute who would be entitled to use the machine by virtue of paragraph (a). A club machine permit shall, by virtue of this subsection, be subject to the conditions— that no child or young person use a Category B or C gaming machine on the club's or institute's premises, and that the holder comply with any relevant provision of a code of practice under section 24 about the location and operation of a gaming machine. For the purposes of subsection (3)(b) a person shall not be treated as the guest of a member if the member extends an invitation— having had no previous acquaintance with the person, and for the purpose only of enabling the person to take advantage of facilities for gaming.

text: The disapplication of section 33 by section 269 or 271 shall not apply to high turnover bingo played during a high turnover period. Bingo played in the course of the activities of a club or institute in any period of seven days is high turnover bingo if— the aggregate of stakes at bingo played during the period in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000, or the aggregate of prizes at bingo played during the period in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000. A high turnover period begins in relation to a club or institute at the end of a period of seven days during which— the aggregate of stakes at bingo played in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000, or the aggregate of prizes at bingo played in the course of the activities of the club or institute exceeds £2,000. A high turnover period expires at the end of the year beginning with the first day of the period of seven days which caused the high turnover period to begin. A period of seven days any of which is in a high turnover period does not cause a new high turnover period to begin. A club or institute in relation to which a high turnover period begins shall, unless the club or institute holds a bingo operating licence, inform the Commission as soon as is reasonably practicable. A club or institute commits an offence if it fails without reasonable excuse to comply with subsection (6). A club or institute guilty of an offence under subsection (7) shall be liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale. The Secretary of State may by order vary a monetary amount specified in this section.

text: In section 279(2) “prescribed” means prescribed by regulations made by the Secretary of State; and regulations may, in particular, make different provision for different classes or descriptions of game. For the purposes of section 279(5) two games are linked if— the result of one game is or may be wholly or partly determined by reference to the result of the other game, or the amount or value of a prize available in one game is or may be wholly or partly determined by reference to the extent of participation in the other game; and if a single game is played partly on one set of premises and partly on another it shall be treated as two linked games.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.280

commentary: S. 280 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: The disapplication of section 33 by section 279 shall not apply to high turnover bingo played during a high turnover period. Bingo played on premises in any period of seven days is high turnover bingo if— the aggregate of stakes at bingo played on the premises during the period exceeds £2,000, or the aggregate of prizes at bingo played on the premises during the period exceeds £2,000. A high turnover period begins in relation to premises at the end of a period of seven days during which— the aggregate of stakes at bingo played on the premises exceeds £2,000, or the aggregate of prizes at bingo played on the premises exceeds £2,000. A high turnover period expires at the end of the year beginning with the first day of the period of seven days which caused the high turnover period to begin. A period of seven days any of which is in a high turnover period does not cause a new high turnover period to begin. The holder of an on-premises alcohol licence or relevant Scottish licence for premises in relation to which a high turnover period begins shall, unless he holds a bingo operating licence, inform the Commission as soon as is reasonably practicable. A person commits an offence if he fails without reasonable excuse to comply with subsection (6). A person guilty of an offence under subsection (7) shall be liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale. The Secretary of State may by order vary a monetary amount specified in this section.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.281

commentary: S. 281 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: Sections 37 and 242 shall not apply to making one or two gaming machines, each of which is of Category C or D, available for use on premises to which this section applies, provided that the conditions in subsections (2) and (3) are satisfied. The first condition is that the person who holds the on-premises alcohol licence or the relevant Scottish licence sends the licensing authority— written notice of his intention to make gaming machines available for use in reliance on subsection (1), and the prescribed fee. The second condition is that any relevant provision of a code of practice under section 24 about the location and operation of a gaming machine is complied with. Subsection (1) does not disapply section 37 or 242 in respect of premises at a time when gaming machines are made available for use on those premises in reliance on a club gaming permit or a club machine permit. In this section “prescribed” means— in the case of premises in respect of which an on-premises alcohol licence has effect, prescribed by regulations made by the Secretary of State, and in the case of premises in respect of which a relevant Scottish licence has effect, prescribed by regulations made by the Scottish Ministers.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.282

commentary: S. 282(2) in force at 1.8.2007 for specified purposes by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(3A), Sch. 3A (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/1157, arts. 3(4), 6, Sch. 2)
S. 282(2) in force at 1.9.2007 in so far as not already in force by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: A person does not commit an offence under section 37 or 242 if he makes a gaming machine of Category C or D available in accordance with a licensed premises gaming machine permit. A licensed premises gaming machine permit is a permit issued by a licensing authority authorising a person to make gaming machines of Category C or D (or both) available for use on premises to which this section applies. A licensed premises gaming machine permit shall, by virtue of this subsection, be subject to the condition that the holder comply with any relevant provision of a code of practice under section 24 about the location and operation of a gaming machine. Subsection (1) does not disapply section 37 or 242 in respect of premises at a time when gaming machines are made available for use on those premises in reliance on a club gaming permit or a club machine permit. Schedule 13, which makes further provision about licensed premises gaming machine permits, shall have effect except in relation to Scotland.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.283

commentary: S. 283(1)(3)(4) in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: A licensing authority may make an order disapplying section 279 or section 282(1) to specified premises. A licensing authority may make an order disapplying a section under subsection (1) only if they think that— the application of the section is not reasonably consistent with pursuit of the licensing objectives, gaming has taken place on the premises in purported reliance on the section but in breach of a condition of that section, the premises are mainly used or to be used for gaming, or an offence under this Act has been committed on the premises. Before making an order under subsection (1) a licensing authority shall— give the holder of the on-premises alcohol licence or of the relevant Scottish licence (“the licensee”) at least 21 days' notice of the authority's intention to consider making an order, consider any representations made by the licensee, hold a hearing if the licensee requests one, and comply with any prescribed requirements for the procedure to be followed in considering whether to make an order. If a licensing authority make an order under subsection (1), they shall as soon as is reasonably practicable give the licensee— a copy of the order, and written reasons for the decision to make the order. A licensee may appeal against the making of an order under subsection (1). An appeal under subsection (5) must be instituted— in the magistrates' court for a local justice area in which the premises to which the appeal relates are wholly or partly situated, by notice of appeal given to the designated officer, and within the period of 21 days beginning with the day on which the appellant receives a copy of the order against which the appeal is brought. On an appeal the magistrates' court may— dismiss the appeal; allow the appeal and quash the order made by the licensing authority; make an order about costs. In relation to premises in Scotland— subsection (6)(a) shall have effect as if it referred to a sheriff within whose sheriffdom the premises are wholly or partly situated, subsection (6)(b) shall not have effect, the reference in subsection (7) to the magistrates' court shall have effect as a reference to the sheriff, and the reference in subsection (7)(c) to costs shall have effect as a reference to expenses. In this section, “prescribed” means prescribed by regulations made by the Secretary of State.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.284

commentary: S. 284 in force at 21.5.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(3), Sch. 3 (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as amended by SI 2007/1157, art. 3(3), 4(2))

text: The Scottish Ministers may, with the consent of the Secretary of State, by regulations provide that such provisions as are set out in the regulations are to apply in relation to— a club gaming permit or club machine permit, in place of Schedule 12 if the applicant for or holder of the permit is the holder of ... a relevant Scottish licence and the premises are premises to which section 125(1) of the Licensing (Scotland) Act 2005 applies, or a licensed premises gaming machine permit, in place of Schedule 13, if the applicant for or holder of the permit is the holder of a relevant Scottish licence and the premises are premises to which section125(1) of the Licensing (Scotland) Act 2005 does not apply, or if the applicant for or holder of the permit falls within such other description as may be specified in the regulations. Regulations under subsection (1) may amend, revoke or otherwise modify any enactment in so far as it appears to the Scottish Ministers necessary or expedient to do so for the purposes of that subsection.

commentary: S. 285 in force at 21.5.2007 for specified purposes by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(2), Sch. 2 (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as amended by S.I. 2007/1157, arts. 3(3), 4)

text: For the purposes of this Act— “fair” means a fair consisting wholly or principally of the provision of amusements, and a fair held on a day in a calendar year is a travelling fair” if provided— wholly or principally by persons who travel from place to place for the purpose of providing fairs, and at a place no part of which has been used for the provision of a fair on more than 27 days in that calendar year.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.286

commentary: S. 286 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: A person does not commit an offence under section 37 or 242 if— he makes one or more Category D gaming machines available for use at a travelling fair, and facilities for gambling (whether by way of gaming machine or otherwise) amount together to no more than an ancillary amusement at the fair.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.287

commentary: S. 287 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: Gaming is prize gaming for the purposes of this Act if neither the nature nor the size of a prize played for is determined by reference to— the number of persons playing, or the amount paid for or raised by the gaming.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.288

text: A person does not commit an offence under section 33 or 37 by providing facilities for prize gaming if— the gaming satisfies the conditions specified in section 293, and the facilities are provided in accordance with a prize gaming permit. A prize gaming permit is a permit issued by a licensing authority authorising a person to provide facilities for gaming with prizes on specified premises. Schedule 14 makes further provision about prize gaming permits.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.289

commentary: S. 289(1) in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

S. 289(3) in force at 21.5.2007 for specified purposes by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(2), Sch. 2 (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as amended by S.I. 2007/1157, arts. 3(3), 4)
S. 289(3) in force at 1.9.2007 in so far as not already in force by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: A person does not commit an offence under section 33 or 37 by providing facilities for prize gaming if— the gaming satisfies the conditions specified in section 293, and the facilities are provided in— an adult gaming centre, or a licensed family entertainment centre. A person does not commit an offence under section 33 or 37 by providing facilities for equal chance prize gaming if— the gaming satisfies the conditions specified in section 293, and the facilities are provided on premises in respect of which a family entertainment centre gaming machine permit has effect.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.290

commentary: S. 290 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: A person does not commit an offence under section 33 or 37 by providing facilities for prize gaming in premises in respect of which a bingo premises licence has effect. A condition may be attached under section 75 or 78 to an operating licence so as— to prevent facilities for a specified description of game from being provided in reliance on subsection (1), or to provide for subsection (1) to apply, whether generally or only in connection with a specified description of game, subject to specified conditions or only in specified circumstances. A condition attached under section 78 by virtue of subsection (2) above may, in particular, relate to a matter listed in section 91(1). Subsection (1) may not be disapplied or modified— by way of a condition attached to an operating licence under section 77, or by way of a condition attached to a premises licence under section 167, 168 or 169.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.291

text: A person does not commit an offence under section 33 or 37 by providing facilities for equal chance prize gaming if— the gaming satisfies the conditions specified in section 293, the facilities are provided at a travelling fair, and facilities for gambling (in whatever form) amount together to no more than an ancillary amusement at the fair.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.292

commentary: S. 292 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: This section specifies the conditions mentioned in sections 289(1), 290(1) and (2) and 292 for prize gaming. The first condition is compliance with such limits as may be prescribed in respect of participation fees (and those limits may, in particular, relate to players, games or a combination; and different limits may be prescribed in respect of different classes or descriptions of fee). The second condition is that— all the chances to participate in a particular game must be acquired or allocated on one day and in the place where the game is played, the game must be played entirely on that day, and the result of the game must be made public— in the place where the game is played, and as soon as is reasonably practicable after the game ends, and in any event on the day on which it is played. The third condition is that a prize for which a game is played, or the aggregate of the prizes for which a game is played— where all the prizes are money, must not exceed the prescribed amount, and in any other case, must not exceed the prescribed value. The fourth condition is that participation in the game by a person does not entitle him or another person to participate in any other gambling (whether or not he or the other person would also have to pay in order to participate in the other gambling). In this section “prescribed” means prescribed by regulations made by the Secretary of State.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.293

commentary: S. 293 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

text: The Secretary of State may by order provide for sections 289, 290 and 292 not to have effect in relation to prize gaming of a specified description.
citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.294

commentary: S. 294 in force at 1.9.2007 by S.I. 2006/3272, art. 2(4)(5), Sch. 3B (with arts. 7-11, 7-12, Sch. 4) (as inserted by S.I. 2007/2169, arts. 3, 6, Sch.)

citation: Gambling Act 2005 (2005 c.19) s.295
